newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money at 3.05/3.07 pct in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: German call money at 3.05/3.07 pct in quiet trade.

text.p: German money markets started the month barely changed, with call money rates trading at around 3.05 to 3.07 percent on Friday.
Activity was very quiet, dealers said, with rates easing just slightly from Wednesday's 3.05 to 3.15 percent range.
German markets were closed on Thursday for the May Day public holiday.

Traders applauded the smooth end to the month, saying that maybe the Bundesbank was making an effort to signal to the future European Central Bank that minimum reserves are an effective way of steering money market operations.
"The Bundesbank wants to show minimum reserves are controllable and an instrument the ECB could use," said one.
"It is great that such a smooth month-end is possible," said another. "It's a shame that it wasn't like this before."

Daily reserve deposits held by commercial banks at the Bundesbank stood at 39.9 billion marks on Wednesday, down from 41.3 billion on Tuesday, while the monthly average was unchanged at 41.1 billion marks.
Borrowing on the Lombard rate totalled around 0.1 billion marks. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) was quoted at 3.10433 percent versus 3.19667 percent on Wednesday.
